recs.stt: Measuring and Improving Your CI/CD Pipelines
recs.x:
I’ve found that his zero-knowledge approach gives me a suite of tests that have high signal when they fail.

Sandi Metz has also spoken extensively on testing, and I particularly like her advice on using mocks in tests appropriately. This talk of hers on the subject comes to mind: [link]

cites.x: Shout out for Sandi Metz book POODR, and her Railsconf talk The Magic Tricks of Testing, if you're a rubyist (though the principles hold true for non-ruby OO programmers too). [link]
Sandy Metz's talk abou what should be tested and that should not: [link]

cites.stt: Ask HN: How much time do you invest in writing tests?
cites.x: I spend about 30% of my time on a new feature writing tests. BTW that is in RoR which the primary language I code in. I would recommend watching this video by Sandi Matz on testing: [link] .
Then you will probably like this: [link]

cites.stt: Ask HN: Do you write tests before the implementation?
cites.x: Not always before, but always eventually and usually once I’m done with “exploration”. Testing done right should be a time saver in the long run!
